sections.title: Linear Tschirnhaus Transform
sections.description: The key algebraic step: eliminating the x⁴ term from a monic quintic.

theorems.name: depressed_quintic_forward
theorems.description: If x is a root of x⁵ + a₄x⁴ + ... = 0, then y = x + a₄/5 is a root of the depressed quintic. Proved via polynomial identity using linear_combination.

theorems.name: depressed_quintic_backward
theorems.description: Inverse direction: root of depressed quintic gives root of original. Same polynomial identity.

theorems.name: depressed_quintic_iff
theorems.description: The Tschirnhaus substitution is a bijection on roots.

sections.title: Full Bring-Jerrard Reduction (Axiomatized)
sections.description: Eliminating x³ and x² terms requires quadratic/cubic Tschirnhaus substitutions.

theorems.name: bringJerrard_reduction
theorems.description: Every depressed quintic can be transformed to Bring-Jerrard form y⁵ + py + q = 0 over ℂ.
theorems.reason: Requires polynomial resultant theory, Kummer extensions not in Mathlib

theorems.name: quintic_to_bringJerrard
theorems.description: Every monic quintic can be reduced to Bring-Jerrard form. Follows from linear transform + axiom.

sections.title: The Bring Radical
sections.description: The unique real root of x⁵ + x + t = 0, providing a 'quintic formula'.

theorems.name: bringRad_strictMono
theorems.description: The function x ↦ x⁵ + x is strictly monotone. Uses Odd.strictMono_pow for x⁵ plus the identity.

theorems.name: bringRad_exists
theorems.description: For every t, x⁵ + x + t = 0 has a real root. Proved via IVT on interval [-(|t|+1), |t|+1].

theorems.name: bringRadical_spec
theorems.description: BR(t)⁵ + BR(t) + t = 0 for all t.

theorems.name: bringRadical_unique
theorems.description: BR(t) is the unique real root of x⁵ + x + t = 0.

theorems.name: bringRadical_anti_mono
theorems.description: BR is strictly decreasing: t₁ < t₂ implies BR(t₁) > BR(t₂).

theorems.name: bringRadical_neg
theorems.description: BR(-t) = -BR(t). The Bring radical is an odd function.

insights: The Tschirnhaus transform proof is a pure polynomial identity (linear_combination suffices)
Strict monotonicity of x⁵ + x follows from Odd.strictMono_pow plus adding the identity
IVT existence proof uses concrete bounds: f(-(|t|+1)) < 0 < f(|t|+1)
The Bring radical is odd and strictly anti-monotone — properties not of radicals but of real functions
Full Bring-Jerrard reduction is the hard part, requiring auxiliary equation solving
